On NUMA systems
column2: a node may start thrashing cache or even swap anonymous

column1: pages while there are still free pages on remote nodes.
This is a result of commits 81c0a2bb515f (""mm: page_alloc: fair zone
allocator policy"") and fff4068cba48 (""mm: page_alloc: revert NUMA aspect
of fair allocation policy"").
Before those changes
column2: the allocator would first try all allowed zones

column1: including those on remote nodes
column2: before waking any kswapds.  But now

column1: the allocator fastpath doubles as the fairness pass
only consider the local node to prevent remote spilling based on
exhausted fairness batches alone.  Remote nodes are only considered in
the slowpath
column2: after the kswapds are woken up.  But if remote nodes still

column1: have free memory
column2: kswapd should not be woken to rebalance the local node

column1: or it may thrash cash or swap prematurely.
Fix this by adding one more unfair pass over the zonelist that is
allowed to spill to remote nodes after the local fairness pass fails but
before entering the slowpath and waking the kswapds.
This also gets rid of the GFP_THISNODE exemption from the fairness
protocol because the unfair pass is no longer tied to kswapd
GFP_THISNODE is not allowed to wake up.
However
column2: because remote spills can be more frequent now - we prefer them

column1: over local kswapd reclaim - the allocation batches on remote nodes could
underflow more heavily.  When resetting the batches
atomic_long_read() directly instead of zone_page_state() to calculate the
delta as the latter filters negative counter values.
